classification.difficultyReason: Models linked running and walking durations, converts time units and equates two expressions for one distance.

content.prompt: George runs twice as fast as he walks. When going to school one day, he walks for twice the time that he runs and takes a total of 20 minutes to get to school.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If $x$ km/h is George’s walking speed, find the distance that he travels to school in terms of $x$.

answer.worked:
George’s running speed is $2x$ km/h. The running and walking times are respectively one-third and two-thirds of the total time.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Running time}&=\frac13\times\frac{20}{60}=\frac19\text{ h}\\\text{Walking time}&=\frac23\times\frac{20}{60}=\frac29\text{ h}\\\text{Distance}&=2x\times\frac19+x\times\frac29\\&=\frac{4x}{9}\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The next day George runs for twice the time that he walks.

children.label: i
children.prompt: If $t$ hours is the time it takes George to get to school, find the distance to school in terms of $x$ and $t$.

answer.worked:
The walking time is $\frac{t}{3}$ hours and the running time is $\frac{2t}{3}$ hours.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance}&=x\times\frac t3+2x\times\frac{2t}{3}\\&=\frac{xt}{3}+\frac{4xt}{3}\\&=\frac{5xt}{3}\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Hence find how many minutes it takes him to get to school on the second day.

answer.worked:
The distance to school is the same on both days, and $x>0$.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{5xt}{3}&=\frac{4x}{9}\\5t&=\frac43\\t&=\frac4{15}\text{ h}\\\text{Time in minutes}&=\frac4{15}\times60\\&=16\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$$
